{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-005/2026-07-27T081403Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/.claude/skills/testing\n\n# Smart Contract Testing\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**You test getters and trivial functions.** Testing that `name()` returns the name is worthless. Test edge cases, failure modes, and economic invariants — the things that lose money when they break.\n\n**You don't fuzz.** `forge test` finds the bugs you thought of. Fuzzing finds the ones you didn't. If your contract does math, fuzz it. If it handles user input, fuzz it. If it moves value, definitely fuzz it.\n\n**You don't fork-test.** If your contract calls Uniswap, Aave, or any external protocol (verified addresses: `addresses/SKILL.md`), test against their real deployed contracts on a fork. Mocking them hides integration bugs that only appear with real state.\n\n**You write tests that mirror the implementation.** Testing that `deposit(100)` sets `balance[user] = 100` is tautological — you're testing that Solidity assignments work. Test properties: \"after deposit and withdraw, user gets their tokens back.\" Test invariants: \"total deposits always equals contract balance.\"\n\n**You skip invariant testing for stateful protocols.** If your contract has multiple interacting functions that change state over time (vaults, AMMs, lending), you need invariant tests. Unit tests check one path; invariant tests check that properties hold across thousands of random sequences.\n\n---\n\n## Unit Testing with Foundry\n\n### Test File Structure\n\n```solidity\n// test/MyContract.t.sol\n// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.20;\n\nimport {Test, console} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {MyToken} from \"../src/MyToken.sol\";\n\ncontract MyTokenTest is Test {\n    MyToken public token;\n    address public alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address public bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        token = new MyToken(\"Test\", \"TST\", 1_000_000e18);\n        // Give alice some tokens for testing\n        token.transfer(alice, 10_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_TransferUpdatesBalances() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        token.transfer(bob, 1_000e18);\n\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(alice), 9_000e18);\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(bob), 1_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_TransferEmitsEvent() public {\n        vm.expectEmit(true, true, false, true);\n        emit Transfer(alice, bob, 500e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        token.transfer(bob, 500e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_RevertWhen_TransferExceedsBalance() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        token.transfer(bob, 999_999e18); // More than alice has\n    }\n\n    function test_RevertWhen_TransferToZeroAddress() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        token.transfer(address(0), 100e18);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Key Assertion Patterns\n\n```solidity\n// Equality\nassertEq(actual, expected);\nassertEq(actual, expected, \"descriptive error message\");\n\n// Comparisons\nassertGt(a, b);   // a > b\nassertGe(a, b);   // a >= b\nassertLt(a, b);   // a < b\nassertLe(a, b);   // a <= b\n\n// Approximate equality (for math with rounding)\nassertApproxEqAbs(actual, expected, maxDelta);\nassertApproxEqRel(actual, expected, maxPercentDelta); // in WAD (1e18 = 100%)\n\n// Revert expectations\nvm.expectRevert();                           // Any revert\nvm.expectRevert(\"Insufficient balance\");     // Specific message\nvm.expectRevert(MyContract.CustomError.selector); // Custom error\n\n// Event expectations\nvm.expectEmit(true, true, false, true);      // (topic1, topic2, topic3, data)\nemit MyEvent(expectedArg1, expectedArg2);\n```\n\n### What to Actually Test\n\n```solidity\n// ✅ TEST: Edge cases that lose money\nfunction test_TransferZeroAmount() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferEntireBalance() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferToSelf() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_ApproveOverwrite() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferFromWithExactAllowance() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ✅ TEST: Access control\nfunction test_RevertWhen_NonOwnerCallsAdminFunction() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_OwnerCanPause() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ✅ TEST: Failure modes\nfunction test_RevertWhen_DepositZero() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_RevertWhen_WithdrawMoreThanDeposited() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_RevertWhen_ContractPaused() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ❌ DON'T TEST: OpenZeppelin internals\n// function test_NameReturnsName() — they already tested this\n// function test_SymbolReturnsSymbol() — waste of time\n// function test_DecimalsReturns18() — it does, trust it\n```\n\n---\n\n## Fuzz Testing\n\nFoundry automatically fuzzes any test function with parameters. Instead of testing one value, it tests hundreds of random values.\n\n### Basic Fuzz Test\n\n```solidity\n// Foundry calls this with random amounts\nfunction testFuzz_DepositWithdrawRoundtrip(uint256 amount) public {\n    // Bound input to valid range\n    amount = bound(amount, 1, token.balanceOf(alice));\n\n    uint256 balanceBefore = token.balanceOf(alice);\n\n    vm.startPrank(alice);\n    token.approve(address(vault), amount);\n    vault.deposit(amount, alice);\n    vault.withdraw(vault.balanceOf(alice), alice, alice);\n    vm.stopPrank();\n\n    // Property: user gets back what they deposited (minus any fees)\n    assertGe(token.balanceOf(alice), balanceBefore - 1); // Allow 1 wei rounding\n}\n```\n\n### Bounding Inputs\n\n```solidity\n// bound() is preferred over vm.assume() — bound reshapes, assume discards\nfunction testFuzz_Fee(uint256 amount, uint256 feeBps) public {\n    amount = bound(amount, 1e6, 1e30);       // Reasonable token amounts\n    feeBps = bound(feeBps, 1, 10_000);       // 0.01% to 100%\n\n    uint256 fee = (amount * feeBps) / 10_000;\n    uint256 afterFee = amount - fee;\n\n    // Property: fee + remainder always equals original\n    assertEq(fee + afterFee, amount);\n}\n\n// vm.assume() discards inputs — use sparingly\nfunction testFuzz_Division(uint256 a, uint256 b) public {\n    vm.assume(b > 0); // Skip zero (would revert)\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\n### Run with More Iterations\n\n```bash\n# Default: 256 runs\nforge test\n\n# More thorough: 10,000 runs\nforge test --fuzz-runs 10000\n\n# Set in foundry.toml for CI\n# [fuzz]\n# runs = 1000\n```\n\n---\n\n## Fork Testing\n\nTest your contract against real deployed protocols on a mainnet fork. This catches integration bugs that mocks can't.\n\n### Basic Fork Test\n\n```solidity\ncontract SwapTest is Test {\n    // Real mainnet addresses — full verified list: addresses/SKILL.md\n    address constant UNISWAP_ROUTER = 0x68b3465833fb72A70ecDF485E0e4C7bD8665Fc45;\n    address constant WETH = 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2;\n    address constant USDC = 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        // Fork mainnet at a specific block for reproducibility\n        vm.createSelectFork(\"mainnet\", 19_000_000);\n    }\n\n    function test_SwapETHForUSDC() public {\n        address user = makeAddr(\"user\");\n        vm.deal(user, 1 ether);\n\n        vm.startPrank(user);\n\n        // Build swap path\n        ISwapRouter.ExactInputSingleParams memory params = ISwapRouter\n            .ExactInputSingleParams({\n                tokenIn: WETH,\n                tokenOut: USDC,\n                fee: 3000,\n                recipient: user,\n                amountIn: 0.1 ether,\n                amountOutMinimum: 0, // In production, NEVER set to 0\n                sqrtPriceLimitX96: 0\n            });\n\n        // Execute swap\n        uint256 amountOut = ISwapRouter(UNISWAP_ROUTER).exactInputSingle{value: 0.1 ether}(params);\n\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // Verify we got USDC back\n        assertGt(amountOut, 0, \"Should receive USDC\");\n        assertGt(IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(user), 0);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### When to Fork-Test\n\n- **Always:** Any contract that calls an external protocol (Uniswap, Aave, Chainlink)\n- **Always:** Any contract that handles tokens with quirks (USDT, fee-on-transfer, rebasing)\n- **Always:** Any contract that reads oracle prices\n- **Never:** Pure logic contracts with no external calls — use unit tests\n\n### Running Fork Tests\n\n```bash\n# Fork from RPC URL\nforge test --fork-url https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY\n\n# Fork at specific block (reproducible)\nforge test --fork-url https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY --fork-block-number 19000000\n\n# Set in foundry.toml to avoid CLI flags\n# [rpc_endpoints]\n# mainnet = \"${MAINNET_RPC_URL}\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## Invariant Testing\n\nInvariant tests verify that properties hold across thousands of random function call sequences. Essential for stateful protocols.\n\n### What Are Invariants?\n\nInvariants are properties that must ALWAYS be true, no matter what sequence of actions users take:\n\n- \"Total supply equals sum of all balances\" (ERC-20)\n- \"Total deposits equals total shares times share price\" (vault)\n- \"x * y >= k after every swap\" (AMM)\n- \"User can always withdraw what they deposited\" (escrow)\n\n### Basic Invariant Test\n\n```solidity\ncontract VaultInvariantTest is Test {\n    MyVault public vault;\n    IERC20 public token;\n    VaultHandler public handler;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        token = new MockERC20(\"Test\", \"TST\", 18);\n        vault = new MyVault(token);\n        handler = new VaultHandler(vault, token);\n\n        // Tell Foundry which contract to call randomly\n        targetContract(address(handler));\n    }\n\n    // This runs after every random sequence\n    function invariant_TotalAssetsMatchesBalance() public view {\n        assertEq(\n            vault.totalAssets(),\n            token.balanceOf(address(vault)),\n            \"Total assets must equal actual balance\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    function invariant_SharePriceNeverZero() public view {\n        if (vault.totalSupply() > 0) {\n            assertGt(vault.convertToAssets(1e18), 0, \"Share price must never be zero\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Handler: guided random actions\ncontract VaultHandler is Test {\n    MyVault public vault;\n    IERC20 public token;\n\n    constructor(MyVault _vault, IERC20 _token) {\n        vault = _vault;\n        token = _token;\n    }\n\n    function deposit(uint256 amount) public {\n        amount = bound(amount, 1, 1e24);\n        deal(address(token), msg.sender, amount);\n\n        vm.startPrank(msg.sender);\n        token.approve(address(vault), amount);\n        vault.deposit(amount, msg.sender);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function withdraw(uint256 shares) public {\n        uint256 maxShares = vault.balanceOf(msg.sender);\n        if (maxShares == 0) return;\n        shares = bound(shares, 1, maxShares);\n\n        vm.prank(msg.sender);\n        vault.redeem(shares, msg.sender, msg.sender);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Running Invariant Tests\n\n```bash\n# Default depth (15 calls per sequence, 256 sequences)\nforge test\n\n# Deeper exploration\nforge test --fuzz-runs 1000\n\n# Configure in foundry.toml\n# [invariant]\n# runs = 512\n# depth = 50\n```\n\n---\n\n## What NOT to Test\n\n- **OpenZeppelin internals.** Don't test that `ERC20.transfer` works. It's been audited by dozens of firms and used by thousands of contracts. Test YOUR logic on top of it.\n- **Solidity language features.** Don't test that `require` reverts or that `mapping` stores values. The compiler works.\n- **Every getter.** If `name()` returns the name you passed to the constructor, that's not a test — it's a tautology.\n- **Happy path only.** The happy path probably works. Test the unhappy paths: what happens with zero? Max uint? Unauthorized callers? Reentrancy?\n\n**Focus your testing effort on:** Custom business logic, mathematical operations, integration points with external protocols, access control boundaries, and economic edge cases.\n\n---\n\n## Pre-Deploy Test Checklist\n\n- [ ] All custom logic has unit tests with edge cases\n- [ ] Zero amounts, max uint, empty arrays, self-transfers tested\n- [ ] Access control verified — unauthorized calls revert\n- [ ] Fuzz tests on all mathematical operations (minimum 1000 runs)\n- [ ] Fork tests for every external protocol integration\n- [ ] Invariant tests for stateful protocols (vaults, AMMs, lending)\n- [ ] Events verified with `expectEmit`\n- [ ] Gas snapshots taken with `forge snapshot` to catch regressions\n- [ ] Static analysis with `slither .` — no high/medium findings unaddressed\n- [ ] All tests pass: `forge test -vvv`\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"49dbc5ad-d42c-4085-b182-532271b0db31","uuid":"971e0859-884f-4dff-8830-f435e20cb788","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:14:48.454Z","isSynthetic":true}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSEECZvJJ4rmH4xjyQB1","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01FWguesYdvixFmwTBPe9NTy","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-005/2026-07-27T081403Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/answer.md","content":"# The vault drift: what the suite proved, and what it only looked like it proved\n\n## The mechanism, first\n\nNo source was provided, so the exact line is inferred from the symptom — but the symptom\npins it down tightly. On withdrawal the vault computes a gross amount for the burned\nshares, charges `WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS`, pays out the net, leaves the fee in the yield\nprotocol — and then debits `totalAssetsStored` by the **gross**:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 gross = _sharesToAssets(shares);\nuint256 fee   = gross * WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS / 10_000;\ntotalAssetsStored -= gross;          // <-- should be `gross - fee`\n_protocolWithdraw(gross - fee, msg.sender);\n```\n\nThe fee physically stays in the protocol (as designed) but is subtracted from the books\nanyway. Each withdrawal strands `fee` wei: real tokens, no shares entitled to them.\n`totalAssetsStored` falls below actual holdings by `Σ fees`, so share price is understated\nfor everyone still in, and later depositors mint against an understated total — they buy in\ntoo cheap and dilute the survivors. Nobody is insolvent; the vault just doesn't know it's\nrich, and the difference is claimable by no one.\n\nWhether it's this exact line or a variant, the *shape* is fixed by the description: a\nper-operation debit that is locally self-consistent and globally non-conservative.\n\n---\n\n## Test by test\n\n### `test_DepositMintsShares`\n\n**Establishes.** For one deposit of the fixture amount into the fixture's starting state,\nthe function's return value and the stored share balance agree, and both equal `999e18`.\nThat's a real check of one thing: the returned value isn't lying about what got written.\n\n**Only appears to establish.** That share-minting math is correct. `999e18` is a magic\nconstant — almost certainly read off the implementation once and pasted back. It has no\nindependent derivation, so it is a change-detector, not an oracle: it can tell you the\nnumber moved, never that the number was right. The property it should assert is a\n*relation* — `shares == assets * totalSupply / totalAssets` (mint at the current price) —\nand it asserts a literal instead.\n\n**Why it stays green under the bug.** It deposits into a virgin vault, where price is 1:1\nand `totalAssetsStored` has not yet had a chance to drift. The harm from the bug — a later\ndepositor minting *too many* shares because the denominator is understated — lives\nprecisely in the state this test never constructs. One deposit into an empty vault is the\none input for which the minting path is bug-immune.\n\n### `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets`\n\nThis is the closest to the real invariant and therefore the most misleading test in the set.\n\n**Establishes.** After one deposit into a fresh vault, the live view `totalAssets()` and the\ncached `totalAssetsStored()` both equal the deposited amount.\n\n**Only appears to establish.** That the cache tracks reality — that the vault's books agree\nwith the tokens it holds. What it checks is agreement *at one sample point, after one\noperation, in the one direction where the fee code never executes*. Agreement-at-a-point is\nthe weakest possible form of a conservation property. The bug is agreement *diverging*, and\ndivergence is a property of a transition, not of a state.\n\nThere is a worse possibility worth checking in the actual source: if `totalAssets()` is\nderived from `totalAssetsStored()` rather than read from the yield protocol, this assertion\ncompares the accounting to itself and **cannot fail under any bug whatsoever**. The oracle\nwould be the contract under test. If so, this test is decorative in the strictest sense.\n\n**The lesson here is the sharpest one in the suite:** they had the right pair of quantities\nand the right form of assertion in hand, and only ever evaluated it in the state where it\ncan't fail.\n\n### `test_WithdrawFeeBps`\n\n**Establishes.** That an immutable/constant returns the literal it was compiled with. In\npractice: that nobody edited one number without editing the other.\n\n**Only appears to establish.** That the fee is tested. It asserts nothing about whether the\nfee is charged, charged once, charged on the correct base, applied to the right side of the\ntransfer, left in the protocol as intended, or — the actual bug — *accounted for*. It would\npass identically if `withdraw()` ignored `WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS` entirely.\n\nThis is the most dangerous green check in the file. It puts the word \"fee\" into the test\nnames and into the coverage report, which is what lets a reviewer scan the list and\nconclude the fee path is covered. It contributes to the *appearance* of the thing it does\nnot test.\n\n### `test_ConstructorSetsUsdt`\n\n**Establishes.** Constructor wiring: the address passed in is the address stored. Marginal\nreal value if the constructor takes several same-typed arguments — it catches an\nargument-order swap.\n\n**Only appears to establish.** Nothing beyond that; it is a test that Solidity assignment\nworks. Zero relevance to this bug. Its operative function in this suite is inflating the\ntest count toward 39 and the function-coverage number toward 100%.\n\n### The common thread\n\nAll four are **single-state assertions after a single operation**, and three of the four\ncompare a value against a literal the implementer chose. Not one asserts a relation between\ntwo states. Not one involves a second holder surviving an operation. All four run against\nthe fresh fixture. The suite has no test that can, even in principle, observe a quantity\ndrifting — because observing drift requires comparing two states, and every assertion here\nlooks at one.\n\n---\n\n## How 100% coverage was compatible with this bug\n\n**Coverage measures execution, not discrimination.** `forge coverage` instruments which\nlines, branches, and functions were *reached*. It has no notion of a wrong line — only an\nunexecuted one. The buggy `totalAssetsStored -= gross` ran in every withdrawal test in the\nsuite and was counted as covered every time. A test that calls `withdraw()` and asserts\nnothing at all produces byte-identical coverage output to one that asserts the full\nconservation law. Coverage is a floor on test quality that any assertion-free test can max\nout.\n\n**100% of lines and functions is a one-dimensional projection of a combinatorial space.**\nThe space that matters for a stateful vault is *sequences of calls × actors × amounts*. The\nsuite covered every edge of the state machine at least once. The bug lives in a **path**:\nwithdraw (leaves residue) → then any subsequent read of price, deposit, or withdrawal by a\nholder who stayed. Full edge coverage says nothing about path coverage, and an accumulation\nbug is by definition invisible at path length 1.\n\n**The bug's magnitude is zero in exactly the states the suite visits.** After one deposit,\ndrift is 0. After a single depositor fully exits, `totalSupply == 0` — the residue exists\nbut there is no survivor to be shortchanged and no meaningful share price to compare\nagainst, so there is nothing to assert a discrepancy *relative to*. Drift only becomes an\nassertable quantity with **≥ 2 holders and ≥ 2 operations**. The suite has neither.\n\n**The diagnostic that would have flagged this immediately is mutation testing, not\ncoverage.** Change `-= gross` to `-= gross - fee` in a scratch branch and re-run: all 39\ntests stay green. Mutation score for that line: 0. Coverage answers \"did we run it\";\nmutation answers \"would we notice.\" Only the second question is about test quality, and the\nsuite was never asked it.\n\nThe lead is right that the suite was thorough along one axis — breadth of call sites\ntouched. It was empty along the axis that mattered — composition of calls. Those two are\nroutinely confused because coverage is the number that gets reported.\n\n---\n\n## Why \"every operation is correct in isolation\" is the tell, not the alibi\n\nBecause it is a restatement of the fact that isolation is the only frame anyone checked.\n\nFormally: for each operation they verified `{P} op {Q}` with a `Q` that was a snapshot —\n\"alice holds 999e18 shares,\" \"totalAssets equals the deposit.\" Then they concluded the\ncomposition of operations was correct. That conclusion is only licensed if `Q` is\n**inductive**: if `Q` holding before an arbitrary next operation implies `Q` holds after it.\nA snapshot postcondition is never inductive — it says nothing about the successor state. So\nthe suite proved a sequence of local facts and inferred a global one that does not follow.\n\nThat inference gap has a signature, and this bug is it. **A defect that is invisible in\nevery single operation but visible in the accumulation is definitionally a violation of a\ncross-call conservation law, not of any per-call spec.** Each withdrawal here genuinely is\ncorrect against its local spec: the user received exactly `gross × (1 − 30bps)`, the shares\nburned matched the quoted rate, and the stored total decreased by exactly the amount the\ncode says it should. There is no call whose postcondition you can point at and call wrong,\nbecause the violated property was never a postcondition of any call. It's a relation\nbetween the sum of what went in, the sum of what came out, and what the vault records —\nand that relation has no owner among the individual functions.\n\nSo \"we cannot point at a single call that misbehaves\" is not evidence the code is fine. It\nis a positive identification of the *class* of bug you have: the composition of correct\nsteps is wrong, which means the error is in what you believed the steps compose to. Nothing\nthat examines steps one at a time can find it. The moment correctness can only be described\none call at a time, you've admitted your postconditions aren't inductive — and the only\ninstrument that closes that gap is a test that composes calls and checks a property across\nthe whole sequence.\n\nWorth noting which property *did* hold: the vault was never insolvent. It held more than it\nthought, never less. That's why this was quiet rather than loud — the one invariant that\nsurvived is the one that would have caused a visible failure. Drift in the safe direction\nis still stolen yield; it just doesn't page anyone.\n\n---\n\n## The property the suite should have asserted\n\nLet, at any point in time:\n\n- `R = totalAssetsStored()` — the vault's recorded total\n- `A = actualAssets()` — assets the vault genuinely controls: its redeemable position in\n  the yield protocol plus any idle token balance, **read from the protocol, never from the\n  vault**\n- `S = totalShares()`, and `P = R × 1e18 / S` for `S > 0` — price per share\n- `D` = cumulative assets deposited; `W` = cumulative assets **actually received by\n  withdrawers** (net of fee), both accumulated by the test from observed token transfers\n\n### I1 — Accounting completeness (catches the bug directly)\n\n> For every state reachable by any sequence of deposits and withdrawals by any set of\n> actors: `R == A`.\n\nEvery asset the vault holds is attributed to some share. No unattributable residue, ever.\nUnder the bug, `A − R == Σ fees` and grows without bound.\n\n### I1′ — Same property, independent oracle (the form to actually ship)\n\n> `R == D − W`, where `D` and `W` are computed by the test harness from observed token\n> flows, not from any view function on the vault.\n\nThis is I1 with the oracle moved outside the contract under test. Because the fee never\nleaves the protocol, \"assets out\" is the *net* amount the user received — so the bug makes\nthis equality fail by exactly the fee on every withdrawal. Critically, it cannot degenerate\ninto a tautology the way `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets` may have.\n\n### I2 — Fee accrual (catches it as the economic harm)\n\n> For every withdrawal that charges a fee `f > 0` and leaves `S_after > 0`:\n> `P_after > P_before`, and specifically `R_after == R_before − netPaidOut`.\n>\n> And for every operation of any kind with `S > 0` on both sides: `P_after >= P_before`.\n\nI1 catches the bug as a bookkeeping mismatch; I2 catches it as *the fee failing to do the\njob it exists for*. Under the bug `P` is flat across fee-charging withdrawals instead of\nrising. Keep both: I2 also catches variants where the accounting is internally consistent\nbut survivors still don't benefit (e.g. the fee getting swept somewhere).\n\n### I3 — Solvency direction (the weak safety net)\n\n> `A >= R` always.\n\nThis one passed throughout. Include it, but note explicitly that it is the invariant that\nheld while the vault was losing money — it is not a substitute for I1.\n\n---\n\n## Test shape\n\nAn invariant harness with a bounded actor pool and ghost variables, plus two cheap unit\nregressions that would have caught this today.\n\n### Handler\n\n```solidity\n// test/invariant/VaultHandler.sol\ncontract VaultHandler is Test {\n    Vault  public vault;\n    IERC20 public usdt;\n    IYieldProtocol public protocol;\n\n    address[] public actors;\n    address   internal currentActor;\n\n    // ghosts — derived from observed token flows, never from the vault's own views\n    uint256 public ghostDeposited;          // D\n    uint256 public ghostPaidOutNet;         // W\n    uint256 public priceFloor;\n\n    uint256 public feeWithSurvivorsCount;   // fee charged AND holders remained\n    uint256 public strictPriceRiseCount;    // ...and their price actually rose\n\n    uint256 public depositCalls;\n    uint256 public withdrawCalls;\n    uint256 public withdrawNoops;\n\n    modifier useActor(uint256 seed) {\n        currentActor = actors[bound(seed, 0, actors.length - 1)];\n        vm.startPrank(currentActor);\n        _;\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    constructor(Vault _vault, IERC20 _usdt, IYieldProtocol _protocol) {\n        vault = _vault; usdt = _usdt; protocol = _protocol;\n        for (uint256 i; i < 4; ++i) {\n            actors.push(makeAddr(string.concat(\"actor\", vm.toString(i))));\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// assets the vault genuinely controls — read from the PROTOCOL, not from the vault\n    function actualAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n        return protocol.balanceOf(address(vault)) + usdt.balanceOf(address(vault));\n    }\n\n    function _price() internal view returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 s = vault.totalShares();\n        return s == 0 ? 0 : vault.totalAssetsStored() * 1e18 / s;\n    }\n\n    function deposit(uint256 seed, uint256 amount) public useActor(seed) {\n        amount = bound(amount, 1e6, 1_000_000e6);\n        deal(address(usdt), currentActor, amount);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), amount);\n\n        uint256 pBefore = _price();\n        vault.deposit(amount);\n\n        ghostDeposited += amount;\n        depositCalls++;\n\n        // depositing must never move the price for existing holders\n        if (pBefore != 0) assertApproxEqAbs(_price(), pBefore, 1, \"deposit moved share price\");\n        _trackPrice();\n    }\n\n    function withdraw(uint256 seed, uint256 pctBps) public useActor(seed) {\n        uint256 held = vault.shareBalance(currentActor);\n        if (held == 0) { withdrawNoops++; return; }\n        uint256 shares = held * bound(pctBps, 1, 10_000) / 10_000;\n        if (shares == 0) { withdrawNoops++; return; }\n\n        uint256 pBefore   = _price();\n        uint256 balBefore = usdt.balanceOf(currentActor);\n\n        vault.withdraw(shares);\n        withdrawCalls++;\n\n        uint256 received = usdt.balanceOf(currentActor) - balBefore;\n        ghostPaidOutNet += received;\n\n        uint256 gross = pBefore * shares / 1e18;   // pre-fee worth of those shares\n        if (gross > received && vault.totalShares() > 0) {\n            feeWithSurvivorsCount++;\n            if (_price() > pBefore) strictPriceRiseCount++;\n        }\n        _trackPrice();\n    }\n\n    function _trackPrice() internal {\n        uint256 p = _price();\n        if (p == 0) { priceFloor = 0; return; }     // vault empty: price undefined, reset\n        assertGe(p, priceFloor, \"share price decreased\");\n        priceFloor = p;\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Invariants\n\n```solidity\n// test/invariant/VaultInvariants.t.sol\ncontract VaultInvariants is Test {\n    uint256 constant ROUNDING_WEI = 10;   // FIXED — must not scale with op count\n\n    Vault vault; MockUSDT usdt; MockYield protocol; VaultHandler handler;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdt     = new MockUSDT();\n        protocol = new MockYield(usdt);\n        vault    = new Vault(usdt, protocol);\n        handler  = new VaultHandler(vault, usdt, protocol);\n\n        targetContract(address(handler));\n        bytes4[] memory sels = new bytes4[](2);\n        sels[0] = VaultHandler.deposit.selector;\n        sels[1] = VaultHandler.withdraw.selector;\n        targetSelector(FuzzSelector({addr: address(handler), selectors: sels}));\n    }\n\n    /// I1\n    function invariant_NoUnattributableResidue() public view {\n        assertApproxEqAbs(\n            vault.totalAssetsStored(), handler.actualAssets(), ROUNDING_WEI,\n            \"recorded total drifted from assets actually held\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// I1'\n    function invariant_StoredMatchesObservedFlows() public view {\n        assertApproxEqAbs(\n            vault.totalAssetsStored(),\n            handler.ghostDeposited() - handler.ghostPaidOutNet(),\n            ROUNDING_WEI,\n            \"stored total != deposits minus net payouts\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// I2\n    function invariant_FeesAccrueToSurvivors() public view {\n        assertEq(\n            handler.strictPriceRiseCount(), handler.feeWithSurvivorsCount(),\n            \"a withdrawal fee was charged but did not raise the survivors' share price\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// I3\n    function invariant_NeverInsolvent() public view {\n        assertGe(handler.actualAssets() + ROUNDING_WEI, vault.totalAssetsStored());\n    }\n\n    /// not an invariant — proves the handler actually exercised the interesting path\n    function invariant_callSummary() public view {\n        console.log(\"deposits          \", handler.depositCalls());\n        console.log(\"withdraws         \", handler.withdrawCalls());\n        console.log(\"withdraw no-ops   \", handler.withdrawNoops());\n        console.log(\"fee-with-survivors\", handler.feeWithSurvivorsCount());\n    }\n}\n```\n\n```toml\n[invariant]\nruns  = 512\ndepth = 100          # drift needs many withdrawals; depth is what makes this a sequence test\nfail_on_revert = true\n```\n\nUnder the bug: **I1, I1′ and I2 go red; I3 stays green.**\n\n### Four things that make or break this harness\n\n1. **Bounded actor pool.** Default invariant fuzzing calls the handler from random fresh\n   `msg.sender` addresses. Every actor would be a first-time depositor and there would\n   never be a *survivor* — the exact precondition the bug needs. Without `useActor`, this\n   whole harness reproduces the blind spot it was written to fix.\n2. **`actualAssets()` must read the protocol, not the vault.** If the test's notion of\n   \"actual\" comes from a vault view function, the invariant is self-referential and worth\n   nothing — the same trap `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets` may already be in.\n3. **Fixed absolute tolerance, never relative.** A 30bps-per-withdrawal drift hides under\n   `assertApproxEqRel(..., 1e16)` for a long time. Use a small fixed wei bound that does not\n   grow with the number of operations; that is what makes accumulation detectable.\n4. **Watch the call summary.** A handler where `withdrawNoops` dominates `withdrawCalls`\n   passes every invariant while testing nothing. Check the counters on the first run.\n\n### Two unit tests that would have caught it today\n\n```solidity\nfunction test_WithdrawFeeRaisesPriceForRemainingHolders() public {\n    _deposit(alice, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n    _deposit(bob,   DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n\n    uint256 priceBefore = _pricePerShare();\n    _withdrawAll(alice);\n\n    assertGt(_pricePerShare(), priceBefore, \"alice's exit fee did not accrue to bob\");\n}\n\nfunction test_StoredTotalTracksHeldAssetsAcrossWithdrawals() public {\n    _deposit(alice, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n    _deposit(bob,   DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n    _withdrawAll(alice);\n\n    // same assertion as test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets — just after the operation\n    // where the two can actually diverge\n    assertEq(vault.totalAssetsStored(), _actualAssets(), \"residue after withdrawal\");\n}\n```\n\nThe second is a one-line generalization of a test they already had. That's the whole gap.\n\n### Acceptance check for the new suite\n\nDo not trust the new invariants because they're green. In a scratch branch, flip the fix\nback (`-= gross - fee` → `-= gross`) and confirm I1, I1′ and I2 go red. If they don't, the\nnew tests are as decorative as the old ones. Then run the same mutation on the *original*\n39 to demonstrate the point about coverage concretely.\n\n---\n\n## One design issue this surfaced\n\n\"Fees accrue to remaining holders\" has a terminal case: the **last** withdrawer's own fee\nbenefits nobody — there are no survivors, and the residue is permanently stranded. So even\nwith correct accounting, `actualAssets()` after a full exit equals the fee on the final\nwithdrawal, not zero. That's a useful sharp discriminator for a test (under the bug it\nequals the sum of *every* fee ever charged), but it's also a real design question worth\ndeciding deliberately rather than inheriting: dust-forever, sweep to owner on last exit, or\nforbid the last holder from being charged.\n\n---\n\n## Unresolved\n\n1. Does `totalAssets()` read the yield protocol, or is it just a getter over\n   `totalAssetsStored`? If the latter, `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets` was structurally\n   incapable of failing and the fix has to start there.\n2. Is the fix retroactive? The stranded balance is real and currently unclaimable — does it\n   get credited back to `totalAssetsStored` at upgrade time (windfall to current holders),\n   or handled some other way?\n3. Deposits: is the same gross/net confusion present on the way in, and is there a deposit\n   fee at all? I only reasoned about the withdrawal path.\n4. Last-out fee (above) — which of the three treatments do you want?\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5132,"cache_read_input_tokens":23935,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5132},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"49dbc5ad-d42c-4085-b182-532271b0db31","uuid":"a46e61f2-c0bd-40c5-a13b-418de57f9186","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:19:01.361Z","request_id":"req_011CdSEEBJGmWtqfwpcJXt1G"}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FWguesYdvixFmwTBPe9NTy","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-005/2026-07-27T081403Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/answer.md (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"49dbc5ad-d42c-4085-b182-532271b0db31","uuid":"24f7c784-7e0b-41bd-81f2-ebf46c65b211","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:19:01.381Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"create","filePath":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-005/2026-07-27T081403Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/answer.md","content":"# The vault drift: what the suite proved, and what it only looked like it proved\n\n## The mechanism, first\n\nNo source was provided, so the exact line is inferred from the symptom — but the symptom\npins it down tightly. On withdrawal the vault computes a gross amount for the burned\nshares, charges `WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS`, pays out the net, leaves the fee in the yield\nprotocol — and then debits `totalAssetsStored` by the **gross**:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 gross = _sharesToAssets(shares);\nuint256 fee   = gross * WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS / 10_000;\ntotalAssetsStored -= gross;          // <-- should be `gross - fee`\n_protocolWithdraw(gross - fee, msg.sender);\n```\n\nThe fee physically stays in the protocol (as designed) but is subtracted from the books\nanyway. Each withdrawal strands `fee` wei: real tokens, no shares entitled to them.\n`totalAssetsStored` falls below actual holdings by `Σ fees`, so share price is understated\nfor everyone still in, and later depositors mint against an understated total — they buy in\ntoo cheap and dilute the survivors. Nobody is insolvent; the vault just doesn't know it's\nrich, and the difference is claimable by no one.\n\nWhether it's this exact line or a variant, the *shape* is fixed by the description: a\nper-operation debit that is locally self-consistent and globally non-conservative.\n\n---\n\n## Test by test\n\n### `test_DepositMintsShares`\n\n**Establishes.** For one deposit of the fixture amount into the fixture's starting state,\nthe function's return value and the stored share balance agree, and both equal `999e18`.\nThat's a real check of one thing: the returned value isn't lying about what got written.\n\n**Only appears to establish.** That share-minting math is correct. `999e18` is a magic\nconstant — almost certainly read off the implementation once and pasted back. It has no\nindependent derivation, so it is a change-detector, not an oracle: it can tell you the\nnumber moved, never that the number was right. The property it should assert is a\n*relation* — `shares == assets * totalSupply / totalAssets` (mint at the current price) —\nand it asserts a literal instead.\n\n**Why it stays green under the bug.** It deposits into a virgin vault, where price is 1:1\nand `totalAssetsStored` has not yet had a chance to drift. The harm from the bug — a later\ndepositor minting *too many* shares because the denominator is understated — lives\nprecisely in the state this test never constructs. One deposit into an empty vault is the\none input for which the minting path is bug-immune.\n\n### `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets`\n\nThis is the closest to the real invariant and therefore the most misleading test in the set.\n\n**Establishes.** After one deposit into a fresh vault, the live view `totalAssets()` and the\ncached `totalAssetsStored()` both equal the deposited amount.\n\n**Only appears to establish.** That the cache tracks reality — that the vault's books agree\nwith the tokens it holds. What it checks is agreement *at one sample point, after one\noperation, in the one direction where the fee code never executes*. Agreement-at-a-point is\nthe weakest possible form of a conservation property. The bug is agreement *diverging*, and\ndivergence is a property of a transition, not of a state.\n\nThere is a worse possibility worth checking in the actual source: if `totalAssets()` is\nderived from `totalAssetsStored()` rather than read from the yield protocol, this assertion\ncompares the accounting to itself and **cannot fail under any bug whatsoever**. The oracle\nwould be the contract under test. If so, this test is decorative in the strictest sense.\n\n**The lesson here is the sharpest one in the suite:** they had the right pair of quantities\nand the right form of assertion in hand, and only ever evaluated it in the state where it\ncan't fail.\n\n### `test_WithdrawFeeBps`\n\n**Establishes.** That an immutable/constant returns the literal it was compiled with. In\npractice: that nobody edited one number without editing the other.\n\n**Only appears to establish.** That the fee is tested. It asserts nothing about whether the\nfee is charged, charged once, charged on the correct base, applied to the right side of the\ntransfer, left in the protocol as intended, or — the actual bug — *accounted for*. It would\npass identically if `withdraw()` ignored `WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS` entirely.\n\nThis is the most dangerous green check in the file. It puts the word \"fee\" into the test\nnames and into the coverage report, which is what lets a reviewer scan the list and\nconclude the fee path is covered. It contributes to the *appearance* of the thing it does\nnot test.\n\n### `test_ConstructorSetsUsdt`\n\n**Establishes.** Constructor wiring: the address passed in is the address stored. Marginal\nreal value if the constructor takes several same-typed arguments — it catches an\nargument-order swap.\n\n**Only appears to establish.** Nothing beyond that; it is a test that Solidity assignment\nworks. Zero relevance to this bug. Its operative function in this suite is inflating the\ntest count toward 39 and the function-coverage number toward 100%.\n\n### The common thread\n\nAll four are **single-state assertions after a single operation**, and three of the four\ncompare a value against a literal the implementer chose. Not one asserts a relation between\ntwo states. Not one involves a second holder surviving an operation. All four run against\nthe fresh fixture. The suite has no test that can, even in principle, observe a quantity\ndrifting — because observing drift requires comparing two states, and every assertion here\nlooks at one.\n\n---\n\n## How 100% coverage was compatible with this bug\n\n**Coverage measures execution, not discrimination.** `forge coverage` instruments which\nlines, branches, and functions were *reached*. It has no notion of a wrong line — only an\nunexecuted one. The buggy `totalAssetsStored -= gross` ran in every withdrawal test in the\nsuite and was counted as covered every time. A test that calls `withdraw()` and asserts\nnothing at all produces byte-identical coverage output to one that asserts the full\nconservation law. Coverage is a floor on test quality that any assertion-free test can max\nout.\n\n**100% of lines and functions is a one-dimensional projection of a combinatorial space.**\nThe space that matters for a stateful vault is *sequences of calls × actors × amounts*. The\nsuite covered every edge of the state machine at least once. The bug lives in a **path**:\nwithdraw (leaves residue) → then any subsequent read of price, deposit, or withdrawal by a\nholder who stayed. Full edge coverage says nothing about path coverage, and an accumulation\nbug is by definition invisible at path length 1.\n\n**The bug's magnitude is zero in exactly the states the suite visits.** After one deposit,\ndrift is 0. After a single depositor fully exits, `totalSupply == 0` — the residue exists\nbut there is no survivor to be shortchanged and no meaningful share price to compare\nagainst, so there is nothing to assert a discrepancy *relative to*. Drift only becomes an\nassertable quantity with **≥ 2 holders and ≥ 2 operations**. The suite has neither.\n\n**The diagnostic that would have flagged this immediately is mutation testing, not\ncoverage.** Change `-= gross` to `-= gross - fee` in a scratch branch and re-run: all 39\ntests stay green. Mutation score for that line: 0. Coverage answers \"did we run it\";\nmutation answers \"would we notice.\" Only the second question is about test quality, and the\nsuite was never asked it.\n\nThe lead is right that the suite was thorough along one axis — breadth of call sites\ntouched. It was empty along the axis that mattered — composition of calls. Those two are\nroutinely confused because coverage is the number that gets reported.\n\n---\n\n## Why \"every operation is correct in isolation\" is the tell, not the alibi\n\nBecause it is a restatement of the fact that isolation is the only frame anyone checked.\n\nFormally: for each operation they verified `{P} op {Q}` with a `Q` that was a snapshot —\n\"alice holds 999e18 shares,\" \"totalAssets equals the deposit.\" Then they concluded the\ncomposition of operations was correct. That conclusion is only licensed if `Q` is\n**inductive**: if `Q` holding before an arbitrary next operation implies `Q` holds after it.\nA snapshot postcondition is never inductive — it says nothing about the successor state. So\nthe suite proved a sequence of local facts and inferred a global one that does not follow.\n\nThat inference gap has a signature, and this bug is it. **A defect that is invisible in\nevery single operation but visible in the accumulation is definitionally a violation of a\ncross-call conservation law, not of any per-call spec.** Each withdrawal here genuinely is\ncorrect against its local spec: the user received exactly `gross × (1 − 30bps)`, the shares\nburned matched the quoted rate, and the stored total decreased by exactly the amount the\ncode says it should. There is no call whose postcondition you can point at and call wrong,\nbecause the violated property was never a postcondition of any call. It's a relation\nbetween the sum of what went in, the sum of what came out, and what the vault records —\nand that relation has no owner among the individual functions.\n\nSo \"we cannot point at a single call that misbehaves\" is not evidence the code is fine. It\nis a positive identification of the *class* of bug you have: the composition of correct\nsteps is wrong, which means the error is in what you believed the steps compose to. Nothing\nthat examines steps one at a time can find it. The moment correctness can only be described\none call at a time, you've admitted your postconditions aren't inductive — and the only\ninstrument that closes that gap is a test that composes calls and checks a property across\nthe whole sequence.\n\nWorth noting which property *did* hold: the vault was never insolvent. It held more than it\nthought, never less. That's why this was quiet rather than loud — the one invariant that\nsurvived is the one that would have caused a visible failure. Drift in the safe direction\nis still stolen yield; it just doesn't page anyone.\n\n---\n\n## The property the suite should have asserted\n\nLet, at any point in time:\n\n- `R = totalAssetsStored()` — the vault's recorded total\n- `A = actualAssets()` — assets the vault genuinely controls: its redeemable position in\n  the yield protocol plus any idle token balance, **read from the protocol, never from the\n  vault**\n- `S = totalShares()`, and `P = R × 1e18 / S` for `S > 0` — price per share\n- `D` = cumulative assets deposited; `W` = cumulative assets **actually received by\n  withdrawers** (net of fee), both accumulated by the test from observed token transfers\n\n### I1 — Accounting completeness (catches the bug directly)\n\n> For every state reachable by any sequence of deposits and withdrawals by any set of\n> actors: `R == A`.\n\nEvery asset the vault holds is attributed to some share. No unattributable residue, ever.\nUnder the bug, `A − R == Σ fees` and grows without bound.\n\n### I1′ — Same property, independent oracle (the form to actually ship)\n\n> `R == D − W`, where `D` and `W` are computed by the test harness from observed token\n> flows, not from any view function on the vault.\n\nThis is I1 with the oracle moved outside the contract under test. Because the fee never\nleaves the protocol, \"assets out\" is the *net* amount the user received — so the bug makes\nthis equality fail by exactly the fee on every withdrawal. Critically, it cannot degenerate\ninto a tautology the way `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets` may have.\n\n### I2 — Fee accrual (catches it as the economic harm)\n\n> For every withdrawal that charges a fee `f > 0` and leaves `S_after > 0`:\n> `P_after > P_before`, and specifically `R_after == R_before − netPaidOut`.\n>\n> And for every operation of any kind with `S > 0` on both sides: `P_after >= P_before`.\n\nI1 catches the bug as a bookkeeping mismatch; I2 catches it as *the fee failing to do the\njob it exists for*. Under the bug `P` is flat across fee-charging withdrawals instead of\nrising. Keep both: I2 also catches variants where the accounting is internally consistent\nbut survivors still don't benefit (e.g. the fee getting swept somewhere).\n\n### I3 — Solvency direction (the weak safety net)\n\n> `A >= R` always.\n\nThis one passed throughout. Include it, but note explicitly that it is the invariant that\nheld while the vault was losing money — it is not a substitute for I1.\n\n---\n\n## Test shape\n\nAn invariant harness with a bounded actor pool and ghost variables, plus two cheap unit\nregressions that would have caught this today.\n\n### Handler\n\n```solidity\n// test/invariant/VaultHandler.sol\ncontract VaultHandler is Test {\n    Vault  public vault;\n    IERC20 public usdt;\n    IYieldProtocol public protocol;\n\n    address[] public actors;\n    address   internal currentActor;\n\n    // ghosts — derived from observed token flows, never from the vault's own views\n    uint256 public ghostDeposited;          // D\n    uint256 public ghostPaidOutNet;         // W\n    uint256 public priceFloor;\n\n    uint256 public feeWithSurvivorsCount;   // fee charged AND holders remained\n    uint256 public strictPriceRiseCount;    // ...and their price actually rose\n\n    uint256 public depositCalls;\n    uint256 public withdrawCalls;\n    uint256 public withdrawNoops;\n\n    modifier useActor(uint256 seed) {\n        currentActor = actors[bound(seed, 0, actors.length - 1)];\n        vm.startPrank(currentActor);\n        _;\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    constructor(Vault _vault, IERC20 _usdt, IYieldProtocol _protocol) {\n        vault = _vault; usdt = _usdt; protocol = _protocol;\n        for (uint256 i; i < 4; ++i) {\n            actors.push(makeAddr(string.concat(\"actor\", vm.toString(i))));\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// assets the vault genuinely controls — read from the PROTOCOL, not from the vault\n    function actualAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n        return protocol.balanceOf(address(vault)) + usdt.balanceOf(address(vault));\n    }\n\n    function _price() internal view returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 s = vault.totalShares();\n        return s == 0 ? 0 : vault.totalAssetsStored() * 1e18 / s;\n    }\n\n    function deposit(uint256 seed, uint256 amount) public useActor(seed) {\n        amount = bound(amount, 1e6, 1_000_000e6);\n        deal(address(usdt), currentActor, amount);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), amount);\n\n        uint256 pBefore = _price();\n        vault.deposit(amount);\n\n        ghostDeposited += amount;\n        depositCalls++;\n\n        // depositing must never move the price for existing holders\n        if (pBefore != 0) assertApproxEqAbs(_price(), pBefore, 1, \"deposit moved share price\");\n        _trackPrice();\n    }\n\n    function withdraw(uint256 seed, uint256 pctBps) public useActor(seed) {\n        uint256 held = vault.shareBalance(currentActor);\n        if (held == 0) { withdrawNoops++; return; }\n        uint256 shares = held * bound(pctBps, 1, 10_000) / 10_000;\n        if (shares == 0) { withdrawNoops++; return; }\n\n        uint256 pBefore   = _price();\n        uint256 balBefore = usdt.balanceOf(currentActor);\n\n        vault.withdraw(shares);\n        withdrawCalls++;\n\n        uint256 received = usdt.balanceOf(currentActor) - balBefore;\n        ghostPaidOutNet += received;\n\n        uint256 gross = pBefore * shares / 1e18;   // pre-fee worth of those shares\n        if (gross > received && vault.totalShares() > 0) {\n            feeWithSurvivorsCount++;\n            if (_price() > pBefore) strictPriceRiseCount++;\n        }\n        _trackPrice();\n    }\n\n    function _trackPrice() internal {\n        uint256 p = _price();\n        if (p == 0) { priceFloor = 0; return; }     // vault empty: price undefined, reset\n        assertGe(p, priceFloor, \"share price decreased\");\n        priceFloor = p;\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Invariants\n\n```solidity\n// test/invariant/VaultInvariants.t.sol\ncontract VaultInvariants is Test {\n    uint256 constant ROUNDING_WEI = 10;   // FIXED — must not scale with op count\n\n    Vault vault; MockUSDT usdt; MockYield protocol; VaultHandler handler;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdt     = new MockUSDT();\n        protocol = new MockYield(usdt);\n        vault    = new Vault(usdt, protocol);\n        handler  = new VaultHandler(vault, usdt, protocol);\n\n        targetContract(address(handler));\n        bytes4[] memory sels = new bytes4[](2);\n        sels[0] = VaultHandler.deposit.selector;\n        sels[1] = VaultHandler.withdraw.selector;\n        targetSelector(FuzzSelector({addr: address(handler), selectors: sels}));\n    }\n\n    /// I1\n    function invariant_NoUnattributableResidue() public view {\n        assertApproxEqAbs(\n            vault.totalAssetsStored(), handler.actualAssets(), ROUNDING_WEI,\n            \"recorded total drifted from assets actually held\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// I1'\n    function invariant_StoredMatchesObservedFlows() public view {\n        assertApproxEqAbs(\n            vault.totalAssetsStored(),\n            handler.ghostDeposited() - handler.ghostPaidOutNet(),\n            ROUNDING_WEI,\n            \"stored total != deposits minus net payouts\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// I2\n    function invariant_FeesAccrueToSurvivors() public view {\n        assertEq(\n            handler.strictPriceRiseCount(), handler.feeWithSurvivorsCount(),\n            \"a withdrawal fee was charged but did not raise the survivors' share price\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// I3\n    function invariant_NeverInsolvent() public view {\n        assertGe(handler.actualAssets() + ROUNDING_WEI, vault.totalAssetsStored());\n    }\n\n    /// not an invariant — proves the handler actually exercised the interesting path\n    function invariant_callSummary() public view {\n        console.log(\"deposits          \", handler.depositCalls());\n        console.log(\"withdraws         \", handler.withdrawCalls());\n        console.log(\"withdraw no-ops   \", handler.withdrawNoops());\n        console.log(\"fee-with-survivors\", handler.feeWithSurvivorsCount());\n    }\n}\n```\n\n```toml\n[invariant]\nruns  = 512\ndepth = 100          # drift needs many withdrawals; depth is what makes this a sequence test\nfail_on_revert = true\n```\n\nUnder the bug: **I1, I1′ and I2 go red; I3 stays green.**\n\n### Four things that make or break this harness\n\n1. **Bounded actor pool.** Default invariant fuzzing calls the handler from random fresh\n   `msg.sender` addresses. Every actor would be a first-time depositor and there would\n   never be a *survivor* — the exact precondition the bug needs. Without `useActor`, this\n   whole harness reproduces the blind spot it was written to fix.\n2. **`actualAssets()` must read the protocol, not the vault.** If the test's notion of\n   \"actual\" comes from a vault view function, the invariant is self-referential and worth\n   nothing — the same trap `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets` may already be in.\n3. **Fixed absolute tolerance, never relative.** A 30bps-per-withdrawal drift hides under\n   `assertApproxEqRel(..., 1e16)` for a long time. Use a small fixed wei bound that does not\n   grow with the number of operations; that is what makes accumulation detectable.\n4. **Watch the call summary.** A handler where `withdrawNoops` dominates `withdrawCalls`\n   passes every invariant while testing nothing. Check the counters on the first run.\n\n### Two unit tests that would have caught it today\n\n```solidity\nfunction test_WithdrawFeeRaisesPriceForRemainingHolders() public {\n    _deposit(alice, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n    _deposit(bob,   DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n\n    uint256 priceBefore = _pricePerShare();\n    _withdrawAll(alice);\n\n    assertGt(_pricePerShare(), priceBefore, \"alice's exit fee did not accrue to bob\");\n}\n\nfunction test_StoredTotalTracksHeldAssetsAcrossWithdrawals() public {\n    _deposit(alice, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n    _deposit(bob,   DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n    _withdrawAll(alice);\n\n    // same assertion as test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets — just after the operation\n    // where the two can actually diverge\n    assertEq(vault.totalAssetsStored(), _actualAssets(), \"residue after withdrawal\");\n}\n```\n\nThe second is a one-line generalization of a test they already had. That's the whole gap.\n\n### Acceptance check for the new suite\n\nDo not trust the new invariants because they're green. In a scratch branch, flip the fix\nback (`-= gross - fee` → `-= gross`) and confirm I1, I1′ and I2 go red. If they don't, the\nnew tests are as decorative as the old ones. Then run the same mutation on the *original*\n39 to demonstrate the point about coverage concretely.\n\n---\n\n## One design issue this surfaced\n\n\"Fees accrue to remaining holders\" has a terminal case: the **last** withdrawer's own fee\nbenefits nobody — there are no survivors, and the residue is permanently stranded. So even\nwith correct accounting, `actualAssets()` after a full exit equals the fee on the final\nwithdrawal, not zero. That's a useful sharp discriminator for a test (under the bug it\nequals the sum of *every* fee ever charged), but it's also a real design question worth\ndeciding deliberately rather than inheriting: dust-forever, sweep to owner on last exit, or\nforbid the last holder from being charged.\n\n---\n\n## Unresolved\n\n1. Does `totalAssets()` read the yield protocol, or is it just a getter over\n   `totalAssetsStored`? If the latter, `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets` was structurally\n   incapable of failing and the fix has to start there.\n2. Is the fix retroactive? The stranded balance is real and currently unclaimable — does it\n   get credited back to `totalAssetsStored` at upgrade time (windfall to current holders),\n   or handled some other way?\n3. Deposits: is the same gross/net confusion present on the way in, and is there a deposit\n   fee at all? I only reasoned about the withdrawal path.\n4. Yield accrual: does `totalAssetsStored` get synced against real protocol yield anywhere?\n   If a `sync()`/`harvest()` exists, it may have been masking or amplifying the drift, and\n   it needs to be a third handler action.\n5. Last-out fee (above) — which of the three treatments do you want?\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

Summary of the argument:\n\n**Per-test.** All four are single-state assertions after a single operation, three comparing against a literal the implementer chose. `test_DepositMintsShares` locks in `999e18` as a change-detector, not an oracle, and only ever runs against a virgin vault — the exact state where minting is bug-immune. `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets` is the near-miss: right pair of quantities, right form, evaluated only after a deposit, the one direction where the fee code never runs (and if `totalAssets()` just reads `totalAssetsStored`, it can't fail at all). `test_WithdrawFeeBps` asserts a constant is a constant while putting \"fee\" in the coverage report. `test_ConstructorSetsUsdt` tests that Solidity assignment works.\n\n**Coverage.** It measures execution, not discrimination — the buggy line ran every time and counted as covered. 100% line/function coverage is edge coverage of the state machine; this bug lives in a path of length ≥ 2 with ≥ 2 holders.
